title_en: Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory v. Wujin Medical Supplies Factory — dispute over damage to legal person's reputation rights
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over right to reputation; first instance; basic people's court; Shanghai; Jiangsu Province; legal person; General Principles of the Civil Law; whether the legal person's right to reputation has been infringed; determination of defamation by fabricating facts; determination of compensation liability; in favor of plaintiff; fabricating facts; product defamation; commercial defamation; right to reputation; dispute over damage to legal person's reputation rights by a products factory
full_text_en:
Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory v. Wujin Medical Supplies Factory — dispute over damage to legal person's reputation rights

Plaintiff: Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory (address: Huashan Road, Shanghai).

Legal representative: Kao Jianguo, factory director of Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory.

Agent ad litem: Xu Shen, cadre of Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory.

Agent ad litem: Song Lianpu, lawyer of Shanghai United Law Firm.

Defendant: Wujin Medical Supplies Factory (address: Zhengping Township, Wujin County, Jiangsu Province).

Legal representative: Hu Zhongwei, factory director of Wujin Medical Supplies Factory.

Agent ad litem: Wang Guozhong, lawyer of Shanghai No. 5 Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Zhonghe, legal worker of Shanghai No. 5 Law Firm.

With respect to the case of plaintiff Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory v. defendant Wujin Medical Supplies Factory concerning dispute over damage to legal person's reputation rights, the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The female sanitary cup is a product developed through cooperation between our factory and the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of Bengbu Medical College. It was formally put into production in 1983, and large quantities were placed on the market in 1984. To promote its own female sanitary cup, the defendant printed a "notice" and mailed it to some pharmaceutical stores and relevant units in Shanghai, and also posted it on the streets. The notice stated that the female sanitary cups produced by Xinya Medical Rubber Factory were overstocked with 1.05 million units, and that they were dumping expired and semi-expired products, and that women who purchased and used them would suffer harm, etc. This is pure fabrication of facts, slandering the quality of the female sanitary cups produced by our factory, damaging our factory's reputation, affecting the sales of the female sanitary cups, and causing certain losses. Therefore, we request that the defendant publish a public apology in the newspaper, eliminate the adverse effects, restore our reputation, apologize, and compensate for losses in the amount of RMB 100,000.

Defendant's Defense: The facts of printing and posting the notice are true. However, to promote its own female sanitary cups, the plaintiff, by convening meetings, placing advertisements, and writing letters to relevant units in Shanghai, slandered the female sanitary cups produced by our factory as toxic, lacking testing methods, and having no product standards, thereby damaging our factory's reputation. For this reason, we counterclaim that the plaintiff should compensate us RMB 100,000, publish a public apology in the newspaper, eliminate the adverse effects, restore our reputation, and clarify the facts to all pharmaceutical stores in Shanghai.

Facts Found by the Court: Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory, in 1980, cooperated with the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of Bengbu Medical College to develop the female sanitary cup. On November 20, 1982, the former Shanghai Rubber Industry Company and the Scientific Research Office of Bengbu Medical College organized experts to conduct technical appraisal of Model I and Model II female sanitary cups, after which batch production commenced. In February 1983, Model II female sanitary cups were placed on the market with good sales. In June 1985, a new product, Model III female sanitary cup, was produced. In February 1986, the defendant printed and distributed hundreds of copies of a "notice" stating that the plaintiff's factory had overstocked 1.05 million female sanitary cups, and that they were dumping expired and semi-expired products. Thereafter, the sales volume of female sanitary cups produced by the plaintiff was affected. Starting in 1986, the annual sales volume dropped from over 600,000 units in 1985 to over 200,000 units. In May and June of that year alone, returns exceeded 70,000 units. From March 1986 to March 1987, returns totaled over 110,000 units. At the current ex-factory price of RMB 1.10 per unit, the tied-up capital exceeded RMB 120,000. In fact, the inventory of female sanitary cups at the plaintiff's factory never exceeded 200,000 units, and at the end of March 1987, the inventory was only 146,311 units. Upon investigation, no units that sold the plaintiff's female sanitary cups ever discovered sales of expired or semi-expired products.

It was further found: The defendant, Wujin Medical Supplies Factory, is a township enterprise, approved and established by the administrative department for industry and commerce in May 1984. On October 29, 1985, it changed its registration to its current legal person name and began primarily operating female sanitary cups. The legal representative, Hu Zhongwei, was originally a worker at the plaintiff's factory, and resigned in June 1984 to work at the defendant's factory. Without technical appraisal by relevant departments, the defendant started producing female sanitary cups in January 1985 and placed large quantities on the market for sale. In October of that year, the plaintiff wrote to the Shanghai Administrative Bureau for Industry and Commerce and other departments, reporting that the defendant's factory had no research unit, no expert appraisal, no product standards, no testing methods, etc., and was placing large quantities of female sanitary cups on the market in violation of quality management regulations, requesting intervention to stop it. It was not until December 3, 1985 that the defendant's female sanitary cups passed appraisal by the Jiangsu Provincial Science and Technology Commission.

On September 24, 1985, the plaintiff, together with the Shanghai Medical Equipment Wholesale Department, convened a meeting of responsible persons from some pharmaceutical stores in Shanghai. According to the testimony of persons who attended the meeting, the plaintiff's factory, in its speech at the meeting, mainly introduced and promoted the new product, Model III female sanitary cup, and never mentioned that the defendant's female sanitary cups were toxic. Regarding the "notice's" allegation that the plaintiff fraudulently used the "antibiotic bottle stopper production license" to pass it off as a production license for female sanitary cups, thereby deceiving distributors and consumers, it was found that the plaintiff had once used the "antibiotic bottle stopper production license" issued by the Ministry of Chemical Industry in 1985 to advertise female sanitary cups. According to state regulations, a production license is not required for the production of female sanitary cups. After the competent authority discovered this, the plaintiff, on December 5 of that year, published a statement in the newspaper.

Opinion of the Court: The reputation rights of enterprises are protected by state law. The state allows enterprises to place qualified products on the market and engage in fair commercial competition. The plaintiff's female sanitary cups have never been overstocked for as long as one year, and there has never been any issue of expired or semi-expired products in their sales; nor has the inventory ever reached 1.05 million units. The defendant, by illegal means, intentionally fabricated facts in the form of a "notice" to slander the female sanitary cups produced by the plaintiff. This conduct violates the provisions of Article 101 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and damages the legal person's reputation rights. The plaintiff's request that the defendant publish a public apology in the newspaper to eliminate the adverse effects, restore its reputation, apologize, and compensate for losses is consistent with Article 120 of the General Principles of the Civil Law and should be supported. However, the decline in sales volume of the plaintiff's female sanitary cups was not solely caused by the defendant's slander; there were also factors such as quality and insufficient promotion. Therefore, the defendant shall compensate the plaintiff for its losses as appropriate. The defendant's production of female sanitary cups without technical appraisal and approval from the competent authority, and its unauthorized placement of large quantities on the market for sale, seriously violates relevant state regulations. The plaintiff's reporting of this to the relevant departments was not improper. As for the defendant's counterclaim that the plaintiff stated at the meeting that the defendant's female sanitary cups were toxic, no evidence was found to support this, and it is not recognized. The Jing'an District People's Court rendered judgment on October 8, 1987, as follows:

1. Within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, the defendant, Wujin Medical Supplies Factory, shall publish a notice in a Shanghai municipal daily newspaper to eliminate the adverse effects for the plaintiff, Shanghai Xinya Medical Rubber Factory, restore its reputation, and issue an apology. The content of the publication shall be subject to review by the court, and the costs shall be borne by the defendant.

2. The defendant shall compensate the plaintiff for losses in the amount of RMB 30,000, to be paid in a lump sum within 10 days after this judgment takes effect.

3. The defendant's counterclaim is dismissed.

The litigation costs of this case, RMB 1,640, shall be borne by the defendant. After the judgment was pronounced, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant filed an appeal.
